aeb57b1336840fd1bf1aeeeaff7fdcfd28f97f61.text: This is the full journey of a VEX document. From a scanner finding, to your assessment of it, to what a customer actually sees.

aed3462c9572a98ead654074d0f427e25babab7c.text: Underneath, the verification plugin reports the individual checks rather than a single opaque verdict.

af9ad6d23e1861f112dc89cd1d08773946ca87c1.text: And the worker that moves data through the pipeline. [pause] Four repositories, four components. The mapping stays that boring on purpose, because the moment it stops matching your repositories, nobody can tell where a vulnerable package actually lives.

b1bb8c8c44936593314ba5e0309441e5c2442c57.text: And there's the verdict, with the reasoning attached rather than a bare yes. [pause] If the answer had been no, you would have that recorded too, which is worth having when somebody asks why you didn't comply.

b1cbf436b1a21859ee0230ef2892b90473f04b49.text: Drill into a component and you get the specifics. The advisory, the package that introduced it, the version that fixes it, and where it stands right now.

b33d22d7e8bbbebbf7b70f3f1474ced960953087.text: If you ship software inside a medical device, the FDA expects an SBOM as part of your premarket submission.

b3a594106a885fa6d8cfdd9c899a251ec749987f.text: Sooner or later a customer asks for your SBOMs, your audit report, and your security contact. Usually as a spreadsheet, usually on a deadline.

b465e6ff740e21e51a8ad5043237c596bfbd36bc.text: The dashboard leads with what actually needs attention, rather than a count of everything that has ever been found.

b5a7f2db2b20e976e1a92795cdd70b98466bd98b.text: Read what it tells you here. [pause] If you're the last owner of a workspace, that workspace goes with you, so hand ownership over first if anyone else still needs it.

b6f4abd78b95ad86eed38c595acd1961e0b5d785.text: It's the cheapest quality gate available. An SBOM that fails here will fail everywhere else too.

b71662c01614a84361c3edf0e331ad03fd21d991.text: Step five reviews the whole thing and shows you where the gaps are.

b73d11c68a3dfc8d6a4fda8528a234b726467389.text: Then the details a downstream consumer would need. A name, an address that identifies a real legal entity, and a way to reach you.

b8b8c77431c1be920f485c5fa47172fb8c63ed33.text: A second contact covers the technical questions, so a scanner integration question does not land in the security inbox.

ba6fb65641844feb4a21ab2723aa35260146b23f.text: The description is worth writing properly. A year from now this release is evidence, and this is the only context anyone gets.

bcff31ee83b038aeabaabff6c732faf83c4cafce.text: Components come first. A component is usually one repository, and it's where the SBOMs themselves end up living. If you have a monorepo, it's whatever you build and version independently.

bd14f2e73a5bdfc9adcd1e66c703c928eb718757.text: But not every finding is exploitable. Most aren't. [pause] The vulnerable code often isn't reachable in the way you actually use the dependency, and VEX is how you say that in a form a machine can read.

bf39a774f2244e72d6c5929b63c8874cb5aeb490.text: Links are simpler. They're where somebody goes when they want the real thing rather than a description of it.

c185ed785eaee56627ce5f35360f22075128121f.text: Step four is what you tell your users. Installation, secure configuration, and how you'll notify them when something changes.

c19d36a053b4849b0be0ea5190550c8fe38ad115.text: Profiles live under Contacts in workspace settings.

c326249c09f389c0939133d887a92252ba9da18a.text: The support period is the part with teeth. Under the CRA you're expected to state it, and to actually honour it for the lifetime you claimed.

c3e69dac2cab0a10613bbffcba582feffc90f3d0.text: Now the part that decides what a visitor actually sees. Visibility is set per component, not once for the whole workspace.

c48dda45a4dfb1a4a659491ce45f4ace812474a8.text: Two of them turn out not to apply, but a scanner has no way of knowing that. [pause] Only you can say whether the vulnerable code is reachable in the way you use it.

c63299cc9d7016f3981c17bf70cfa31b5db861b9.text: And you decide what goes public. Per product, per component. [pause] Public, private, or gated behind an NDA a visitor signs before the detail opens up.

c73019e3d8c4182f1025f9638641035f93ae1ef2.text: You can also attach a company NDA. That's what makes gated access possible later, where somebody signs before they see the detail.

c8beff976e21bb208a720d493f1e46c361f96816.text: security dot txt is worth enabling while you're here. It's the standard file a researcher looks for when they need to report something, and sbomify keeps it in sync with your contact profile.

caddfaa7a1a2746d1303fada7482e6836b8c756a.text: OSV is the open source vulnerability database, and it's free on every plan. [pause] Flip it on and sbomify starts matching your components against it.

cb03a342d4e7e7d52e446ed1e14c99f3ec1d2d67.text: Same collapsed danger zone as everywhere else, and the same reason for it. Nothing destructive is one stray click away.

cbbe172dcde12f9d1ca47374b233d0787129d6f1.text: The roles matter more than they look. [pause] Manufacturer, supplier and author are distinct ideas in the SBOM formats, and here the same company is all three.

cc7b6d4df7b792c1aae2680abab5c6baff0d6039.text: Last is the lifecycle, and it's the section people skip.

d0bc1353a289cf31349d5d6bb21dab3922cb97a1.text: Scroll down and there's already a release here, called Latest. sbomify maintains that one for you, and it always points at the newest SBOM for every component.

d0cf74a3c85963daa732df7b550efe5e1a47677c.text: Switching it on tells sbomify to match every SBOM you've uploaded against OSV's data. [pause] It runs against what is already stored, so nothing needs re-uploading, and it keeps running as new SBOMs arrive.

d0efe721c2067796e31ef64fc01c252bf34ef170.text: And private keeps it out of the trust center entirely.

d1b2513f97081f10c991d4ffc85121f410793485.text: The usual way to upload an SBOM from CI is to mint an API token and paste it into your repository secrets. It works, and it's also the thing that leaks.

d3606f56dd66bf25bcd74909bc5f82d34fdf9eb8.text: You name the repository allowed to publish here. That's the entire configuration. [pause] No token is created, because there's nothing to create.

d43120f8b917e7881af749d77d4507c7ba512d35.text: So drop in a CycloneDX VEX document. It's a standard format, which means the statement you're about to make travels to anyone downstream without them having to trust a bespoke report.

d49d029e099ef7afd8d585127235a04d9dd72dfe.text: Before sbomify can tell you anything useful, it has to know how your software is actually put together. So let's build that up from nothing, the way you would on your first day.

d58847c87e46c7f20433b5d75f702169f68867ba.text: A product is the thing you actually sell. It holds no files itself. It gathers up the components that make it real, which is why you can ship the same library in three products without maintaining three copies of anything.

dc2b28d8a0c5e3e223d6f344138c366a3ad2a148.text: The badges sit on the SBOM's own page rather than the component summary, because they describe this exact file and this exact version of it.

dce3cc1f3d3e1aaecd0b7efec722d55dd65725e1.text: Confirm, and the workspace is gone. [pause] If you only wanted to hand it to someone else, transfer ownership instead. That keeps the artifacts and the history intact.

e21060aaf3cc17eca2cbabda2b7a334fb623fb10.text: Instead of a customer downloading your SBOMs by hand every quarter, their systems discover and pull them automatically, using a standard neither of you had to invent.

e45756647f4ddbaeafb0226e2829ff83a32b6a7a.text: Apply it, and only now is anything written.

e4df763d8e142db34c523186384324919fd6b0af.text: It won't file the submission for you, but it does mean the SBOM half of it stops being a surprise.

e7d8f94052f32b97d23c3969a1e6edd287e7e95f.text: So open it up and start attaching artifacts to it.

e860420022efc479a1cd4f77008b9d4a1983ae73.text: Give the profile a name you'll recognise later. Most teams need only one, so marking it the default means it applies without anyone choosing it.

e87e9ffc7fd2ebd4f1e5d909fc06c4cd42d4a242.text: Public means anyone with the link can see it, and it's the right setting for the SBOM of something you already ship openly.

e90ce12756851ec0e480cbd0f56fc8f6ebdcf91d.text: Findings land against the component that introduced them, so you're told which repository to go and fix, rather than handed a flat list of package names with no owner.

ea5f24dea5c88caebcf08133f2efde63da4cae84.text: This one marks a high severity finding as not affected, because the vulnerable code path is never reachable. You can see the counts move before you commit to it.

eef16e5e884695f29c81c779d28ae5d2c8612df6.text: A contact can hold more than one role, and here the same person is the author and the technical contact as well.

f01037d8a3ffeeb8bd465b124fb359a6877b7fed.text: And a package URL points at where the thing actually comes from. Between the two, an automated scanner has a fighting chance of matching an advisory to this exact product rather than something with a similar name.

f04f75f5b6204ee75b8151f1a0530408ab804b1d.text: OSV is the open source vulnerability database, and it's the one to start with, because it costs nothing on any plan.

f25967f17b9dec93a9dad56aad00a9e71769cba5.text: Each component carries its own artifacts. SBOMs, VEX documents, and the compliance paperwork that goes with them.

f299fc9c6d027c0239a57f3e884813d07201bc62.text: A release pins an exact set of those artifacts to a version you actually shipped.

f46c5656b62143d95ef1a7ed7aa9c1ec59add48a.text: Rather than retyping that on every upload, you describe it once as a contact profile, and sbomify stamps it onto the SBOMs as they arrive.

f4a84a1d8c09f712034d9b333a69da5851ee5e79.text: The important part is the justification. Not just a claim, but a stated reason a reviewer can argue with. This one says the vulnerable code path is never reached.

f4dac9bdbd88ab25b165751e7cc8930643e2c556.text: A trust center answers that in advance. It's a public page backed by the artifacts already in your workspace, so nothing has to be assembled by hand.

fb16831a6c65063f8832995959e76caaa07d54d1.text: It lives in workspace settings, at the bottom, behind a collapsed danger zone. That's deliberate. Nobody reaches it by accident.

fca0643e8dcf6d6b29d9a47e92bc118d0bf578ca.text: The trust is bound to a single component, so a compromised workflow can only ever write to the one thing it was authorised for.

ff828eea3b65210810c1e5398aa47775d51de231.text: Scanners are plugins, and they run against the SBOMs you've already uploaded. Nothing needs re-uploading to turn one on.

ff874da96394e090de8c69e7903064143bfbb426.text: The Cyber Resilience Act applies to almost anything with digital elements sold into the European Union, and it arrives with real deadlines.

fffcd8b9d8b3d8e4742d2018a86e4140c107f2f3.text: Trusted publishers live behind the component's menu.
